commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Only create draft_id_to_target_id when draft vocab differs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

We found a bug that makes full-vocab EAGLE3 drafters (`draft_vocab_size == target vocab_size`, e.g. `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` and `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Eagle3`) run a redundant vocab-remapping step after the lm_head, degrading decode performance with no effect on the output.

`compute_logits` in `llama_eagle3.py` has a fast path and a slow path. Full-vocab drafts were meant to take the fast path, but erroneously they never do. On H20, the slow path's `logits_new[:, targets] = logits` is `5x` slower than a plain copy:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py::Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM
def compute_logits(self, hidden_states):
    logits = self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)
    if self.draft_id_to_target_id is None:
        # full-vocab draft: logits are already in target vocab space
        return logits

    # reduced-vocab draft: scatter into target vocab space
    base = torch.arange(self.config.draft_vocab_size, device=logits.device)
    targets = base + self.draft_id_to_target_id
    logits_new = logits.new_full(
        (logits.shape[0], self.config.vocab_size), float("-inf")
    )
    logits_new[:, targets] = logits
    return logits_new
```

In `__init__`, even when `draft_vocab_size == target vocab_size`, the parameter is still initialized — it is never `None`, so the slow path is always taken:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py::Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM
def __init__(self, ...):
    ...
    self.draft_id_to_target_id = nn.Parameter(
        torch.zeros(self.config.draft_vocab_size, dtype=torch.long),
        requires_grad=False,
    )
    ...
```

After reading https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18488 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18909, we believe full-vocab drafts were always meant to take the fast path.

This is corroborated by `qwen3_dspark.py` and `qwen3_dflash.py`, which already handle it correctly:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py::Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM
def __init__(self, ...):
    ...
    target_vocab_size = vllm_config.model_config.get_vocab_size()
    if self.config.draft_vocab_size != target_vocab_size:
        self.draft_id_to_target_id = nn.Parameter(
            torch.zeros(self.config.draft_vocab_size, dtype=torch.long),
            requires_grad=False,
        )
    else:
        self.draft_id_to_target_id = None
    ...
```

So we follow dspark/dflash: create the parameter only when the draft vocab differs. Full-vocab drafts then take the `is None` fast path and return the lm_head logits as-is (bit-identical); reduced-vocab drafts are unaffected.

## Test Plan

1. Added a print to the slow path of `compute_logits` and ran a full-vocab EAGLE3 draft, before and after the change.
2. Added a unit test for the conditional: `pytest tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py -k d2t -v`
3. End-to-end speculative-decoding acceptance run on an H20 GPU with `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Eagle3` (`num_speculative_tokens=3`), using 80 MT-Bench prompts passed through the chat template, before and after the change, measuring the acceptance rate.

## Test Result

1. Before the change, the print fires on every call; after the change, it never fires — the slow path is confirmed not taken, and the slow operation is avoided.
2. The unit test passes; the two full-vocab cases fail on unpatched code, so it guards the regression.
3. Before the change:

   ```
   total_num_output_tokens: 20480
   num_drafts: 12294
   num_draft_tokens: 36882
   num_accepted_tokens: 8171
   mean acceptance length: 1.66
   --------------------------------------------------
   acceptance at token 0: 0.41
   acceptance at token 1: 0.18
   acceptance at token 2: 0.08
   ```

   After the change:

   ```
   total_num_output_tokens: 20480
   num_drafts: 12294
   num_draft_tokens: 36882
   num_accepted_tokens: 8171
   mean acceptance length: 1.66
   --------------------------------------------------
   acceptance at token 0: 0.41
   acceptance at token 1: 0.18
   acceptance at token 2: 0.08
   ```

   Every counter matches exactly across both runs, confirming the change is output-neutral for full-vocab drafts.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, GLM-5.3) and reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Gemma 4] Don't read fft_length when profiling unified audio
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`Gemma4DummyInputsBuilder.get_dummy_mm_data` reads `processor.feature_extractor.fft_length` unconditionally to size the dummy audio item:

```python
if num_audios > 0:
    audio_len = processor.feature_extractor.fft_length
```

`Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor.__init__` sets `self.fft_length`. `Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor` defines no such attribute, so the unified (encoder-free) Gemma 4 variant fails during memory profiling, before the engine finishes starting:

```
AttributeError: 'Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor' object has no attribute 'fft_length'
```

## Why it is latent rather than always-on

The line is only reached when audio is the modality with the largest per-item token count, because `compute_mm_encoder_budget` takes a `max()` over `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` and profiles that one modality alone. With the shipped defaults audio loses:

| modality | per-item tokens |
|---|---|
| image | 280 |
| audio | 750 (`audio_seq_length`) |
| video | 2496 (32 frames x 78) |

Video wins, the dummy video branch runs, and the audio line never executes. So a default deployment boots fine.

It stops booting as soon as `audio_seq_length` is raised above the video budget — which is exactly what you do to serve audio longer than 30 s on this variant, since `_compute_audio_num_tokens` ends in `return min(t, audio_seq_length)` and the mel framing yields 25 tokens/s, so 750 tokens is 30.0 s. Raising the ceiling makes audio win the `max()`, the profiler switches to the audio branch, and the engine no longer starts.

## The change

```python
feature_extractor = processor.feature_extractor
if isinstance(feature_extractor, Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor):
    return feature_extractor.fft_length

sampling_rate = feature_extractor.sampling_rate
max_duration_s = processor.audio_seq_length * processor.audio_ms_per_token / 1000.0
return int(max_duration_s * sampling_rate)
```

`audio_seq_length` and `audio_ms_per_token` are the same pair this file already uses to warn about over-long audio in `_call_hf_processor`, so the dummy item is sized to the worst case the model will actually accept. Behaviour is unchanged for `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor`.

## Test Plan

Two unit tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py`:

- an extractor that is not a `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor` sizes the dummy audio from the declared budget (3000 tokens x 40 ms at 16 kHz = 1,920,000 samples);
- a `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor` subclass still returns its `fft_length`.

## Test Result

Please treat this section as a statement of what I could and could not run.

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files.
- The two new tests have **not** been executed. The environment I have does not ship `transformers.models.gemma4`, so that test module cannot even be collected here, and CI on this PR has not run — `pre-run-check` gates it on a label or four merged PRs, and I have neither.
- What I did verify directly is the branch logic, by evaluating `_dummy_audio_num_samples` in isolation against both shapes: the fallback returns `1,920,000` for a 3000-token budget at 16 kHz, and the `fft_length` path returns its value unchanged.

An earlier revision of this description said the tests pass. That was wrong and I have corrected it rather than leave it standing.

## Note for reviewers

Using `fft_length` as a *sample count* for the dummy audio looks questionable on the tower path too — it is an FFT window size (`2 ** ceil(log2(frame_length))`, so typically a few hundred samples), which makes the dummy item far shorter than the audio the model accepts and profiling reserves correspondingly little. I have deliberately not changed that here, to keep this PR to the crash. Happy to follow up separately if maintainers agree it is worth addressing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][MoE] Avoid uninitialized EPLB state in DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark drafter
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark startup when EPLB is enabled for the target model.

The target and DSpark draft use different routed-expert topologies (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash target: 384 routed experts; DSpark drafter: 128). When target-model EPLB is enabled, the draft routers inherit `enable_eplb=True`, but the drafter is not registered with a compatible EPLB model state. Its router-level `EplbLayerState` therefore never receives `expert_load_view` / logical-to-physical mappings and profiling fails with:

```text
ValueError: EPLB requires expert_load_view != None
```

## Fix

- Keep EPLB enabled for the target model.
- Apply the override in the shared `load_dspark_model()` path while constructing the draft `ParallelConfig`.
- Use shallow config `replace()` calls only; do not deep-copy the full `VllmConfig` after target-model construction.
- Disable draft EPLB, redundant experts, and elastic EP atomically in the same `ParallelConfig` replacement.
- Preserve the target config and shared runtime/compilation state.
- Add a focused regression test for atomic target/draft parallel-config isolation.

This intentionally disables EPLB for DSpark draft models while leaving target EPLB unchanged. Full heterogeneous target/draft EPLB support belongs in the EPLB multi-model machinery and should be handled separately.

## Validation

Focused regression test:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
# 1 passed
```

Revalidated on the original 8x NVIDIA H20 environment:

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- TP8 / EP8
- NVIDIA driver: 595.58.03
- CUDA: 13.2
- Target EPLB enabled
- DSpark speculative decoding enabled with 5 draft tokens

Observed after the patch:

```text
Using ['PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends for group 'eplb:0'
EPLB is disabled for the DSpark draft model. EPLB remains enabled for the target model.
EPLB is enabled for MoE part of model /models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Initialized EPLB communicator: NixlEplbCommunicator.
DSpark draft model loaded: 97 params
Rearranged experts (profile) in 1.09 s.
OpenAI server is ready to accept requests
```

A real completion request succeeded with speculative decoding active:

```text
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total 5
vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total 25
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total 16
```

No `deepcopy`/pickling, EPLB-state, CUDA, or EngineCore errors occurred.

For transparency, the H20 runtime validation used the production DeepSeek image with this loader change backported rather than a full binary rebuild of the PR head. The focused regression test was run against the PR implementation.

Model-evaluation impact: not applicable to model numerics or output semantics; this only changes the draft parallel configuration used during DSpark model construction.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open vLLM PRs for `DSpark EPLB DeepSeek V4.1`, `expert_load_view DSpark`, and `expert_load_view EPLB speculative`; no other open PR addresses this startup failure. Issue #50576 concerns SM8x/Ampere DSpark support and is unrelated. Related precedent: #25311 added multi-model EPLB support for MoE speculative models with compatible expert topology.

## Trade-off

The DSpark draft MoE does not receive EPLB balancing with this workaround. The target model remains EPLB-enabled, preserving the primary EPLB benefit while avoiding the startup correctness failure.

## AI Assistance

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with root-cause analysis, patch drafting, regression-test drafting, and PR text refinement. The submitter supplied the production H20 reproduction environment and failure logs, reviewed every changed line, ran the focused test, and performed the H20 validation described above. AI assistance is also recorded in the commit trailers.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Nemotron] Skip redundant latent-MoE all-reduce at TP>1 (~13% decode win)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

**Nemotron-3 decode regressed ~14% between v0.26.0 and v0.27.x at TP>1. This PR restores it.** The mechanism is generic but `NemotronH` is the only model that opts in, so it is the only one whose behaviour changes. No existing issue found.

| tp4, concurrency 1, inter-token latency | v0.26.0 | v0.27.1 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Super 120B-A12B BF16 (n=4/arm) | 4.07 ms | 4.64 ms (**+13.8%**) | **4.08 ms** (+0.15%) |
| Ultra 550B-A55B NVFP4 | 6.86 ms† | 7.21 ms | **6.79 ms** (−5.8% same-node) |

† cross-node, directional only — see Test Result.

### Root cause

[`_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L434-L453) (added in v0.27.0rc1) all-reduces the routed output in latent space before the transform is applied, and [the combined output is all-reduced again](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L455-L495) on the late path ([call site](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L742-L749)).
So **every latent-MoE layer at TP>1 or EP>1 issues two tensor-parallel all-reduces per token instead of one.** The function does not exist in v0.26.0.
`NemotronH` is hit because it passes [`fc2_latent_proj` as its `routed_output_transform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L226).

### The fix

Adds an opt-in `reduce_commutative` attribute, **defaulting to `False` so every model that does not set it is byte-for-byte unchanged.**
`NemotronH` sets it when the transform is bias-free **and** unquantised — then `sum_r W x_r == W sum_r x_r`, so reducing once *after* the transform is equivalent and costs one collective instead of two.
Quantisation is judged from the **constructed layer**, not the model-wide `quant_config`: ModelOpt excludes the latent projections, so a quantised Nemotron-3 checkpoint has `quant_config != None` yet still gets an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` here. Testing the model-wide config would disable this on exactly the quantised checkpoints where the regression is largest.

**Kimi K3 is unchanged.** Its [`KimiRoutedOutputTransform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py#L295-L302) wraps an `RMSNorm`, never sets the flag, and keeps both collectives.

<details>
<summary>Interactions checked, and the alternative considered</summary>

- [`skip_final_all_reduce`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L468-L473) asserts against [`_fused_output_is_reduced`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L403-L408), a combine-kernel property this PR does not touch.
- For `NemotronH`, `reduce_results` defaults to `True` — the [`reduce_results=False`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L180) nearby is on *shared_experts*, not the FusedMoE — so the late all-reduce always fires.
- Runtime check on Ultra NVFP4: `quant_config=ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` (non-None) while `fc2_latent_proj.quant_method=UnquantizedLinearMethod`, confirming the layer-level test is the correct one.
- Alternative: [`LatentMoERunner`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L52) already fuses to one collective, but it now lives under `vllm/models/kimi_k3/` (moved by [#50678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50678)) and reads [`transform.norm`/`up_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L216-L224), which `NemotronH` does not have. Happy to go that way if preferred.

</details>

## Test Plan

4x GB300 (sm_103), stock upstream containers `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0` and `:v0.27.1`, no NCCL env overrides. Public checkpoints [Super BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16) and [Ultra NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4). Every flag exists in both releases, so arms differ only by vLLM version; the `+ this PR` arms patch the same container in place.

```bash
vllm serve <ckpt> --served-model-name nemotron --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 2200 --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --attention-backend FLASHINFER --trust-remote-code --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384

aiperf profile --url localhost:8000 --model nemotron --tokenizer <ckpt> \
    --endpoint-type completions --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --streaming \
    --extra-inputs "min_tokens:1000" --extra-inputs "max_tokens:1000" \
    --extra-inputs "ignore_eos:true" --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 1000 \
    --output-tokens-mean 1000 --concurrency $C --request-count $((5*C)) --warmup-request-count 1

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \
    --model_args model=nemotron,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=<ckpt>
```

## Test Result

### Super BF16, tp4, c=1 — four samples per arm, two server loads each

| arm | ITL (ms) | n | spread | tok/s per user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 4.07 | 4 | 0.03 | 245.56 |
| v0.27.1 | **4.64** | 4 | 0.02 | 215.73 |
| + this PR | **4.08** | 4 | 0.01 | 245.21 |

Regression **+13.8% ITL / −12.2% tok/s**; with this PR **+0.15% vs v0.26.0**. The v0.26.0 and patched arms ran on *different* nodes and still agree to 0.15%.

### Concurrency sweep, Super BF16 (single run per point)

| ITL (ms) | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 4.08 | 6.23 | 9.88 | 12.18 |
| v0.27.1 | 4.60 | 6.63 | 10.39 | 13.09 |
| + this PR | **4.07** | **6.11** | **9.88** | **12.21** |

Restored at every concurrency. The win shrinks as batch grows — at small batch the collectives are latency-bound so their *count* dominates; at large batch they are bandwidth-bound and the surviving reduce (4096-wide) exceeds the removed one (1024-wide). Not a trade-off at any measured point.

### Ultra NVFP4, tp4, c=1 — confirms the fix on a quantised checkpoint

| arm | ITL (ms) | n | tok/s per user | vs v0.26.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.26.0 | 6.86 | 3 | 145.68 | — |
| v0.27.1 | 7.21 | 2 | 138.71 | +5.0% |
| + this PR | **6.79** | 3 | **147.22** | **−1.1%** |

**v0.27.1 → +this PR is same-node, same-container: −5.8% ITL / +6.1% tok/s.** That is the quantitative claim here.
Read the v0.26.0 row directionally: it is cross-node, and this checkpoint shows ~8% node-to-node variation (v0.27.1 stock measured 7.78 and 7.20 ms on two nodes, stable within each, identical clock/power caps — likely co-tenancy on the 72-GPU chassis). Super BF16 has no such issue, reproducing to 0.03 ms across four nodes.

### Controls

| control | result |
|---|---|
| tp1 negative control (early reduce is TP-gated) | 6.22 vs 6.20 ms, **−0.3% — no difference** |
| node-to-node variation, Super BF16 | 4.63 vs 4.60 ms, **0.65%** |

### Accuracy — gsm8k, 5-shot, greedy, tp4, full 1319 questions

| checkpoint | arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| Super BF16 | v0.27.1 | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9181 ± 0.0076 |
| Super BF16 | + this PR | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9166 ± 0.0076 |
| Ultra NVFP4 | v0.27.1 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | 0.9340 ± 0.0068 |
| Ultra NVFP4 | + this PR | 0.9431 ± 0.0064 | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 |

All four deltas within one standard error. Bitwise identity is not expected — moving the all-reduce past a linear map changes float summation order. The Ultra pair covers the quantised case this PR newly enables.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Measure complete pooling responses
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Pooling benchmarks recorded E2E latency as soon as response headers arrived. JSON responses were subsequently consumed during parsing, but binary `bytes` responses were never consumed, so their reported latency excluded response transfer and the connection could be closed while the server was still writing. The newer `bytes_only` format was also treated as JSON and every request failed.

This change consumes the complete response before recording latency. Binary bodies are drained incrementally without retaining the embedding payload in memory. The existing metadata header remains the source of token usage for `bytes`; because `bytes_only` intentionally has no metadata, it falls back to the benchmark's client-side prompt length.

## Reproducer

Start an MRV2 pooling server:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  vllm serve intfloat/e5-small-v2 \
  --runner pooling \
  --dtype float16 \
  --max-model-len 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --port 8911
```

Run the benchmark once per encoding format:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-embeddings \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8911 \
  --model intfloat/e5-small-v2 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 128 \
  --random-output-len 1 \
  --num-prompts 32 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --extra-body '{"encoding_format":"bytes_only"}'
```

Replace `bytes_only` with `bytes` or `float` to exercise the other response paths.

## Output on main

A direct main-versus-branch invocation of the request helper against the same live MRV2 server produced:

```text
main float success= True latency_ms= 15.603 prompt_len= 4 error=
main bytes success= True latency_ms= 8.372 prompt_len= 4 error=
main bytes_only success= False latency_ms= 8.671 prompt_len= 0 error= 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: application/octet-stream', url='http:
```

A deterministic server that sends headers immediately and delays its body by 250 ms also showed that main reported only header latency and abandoned the binary body:

```text
float success= True reported_latency= 0.0017 wall= 0.2526 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes success= True reported_latency= 0.0005 wall= 0.0006 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes_only success= False reported_latency= 0.0008 wall= 0.2534 prompt_len= 0 error= 200, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: application/octet...
```

## Output on this branch

```text
branch float success= True latency_ms= 12.401 prompt_len= 4 error=
branch bytes success= True latency_ms= 12.815 prompt_len= 4 error=
branch bytes_only success= True latency_ms= 12.648 prompt_len= 2 error=
```

The same deterministic delayed-body check now includes the full transfer time for all formats:

```text
float success= True reported_latency= 0.2525 wall= 0.2526 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes success= True reported_latency= 0.2512 wall= 0.2513 prompt_len= 7 error=
bytes_only success= True reported_latency= 0.2513 wall= 0.2513 prompt_len= 11 error=
```

`bytes_only` prompt-token accounting is intentionally client-estimated because that wire format omits server metadata; this does not affect request success or latency.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -q
# 18 passed in 0.81s
```

| Endpoint | Format | Requests | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `/v1/embeddings` | `float` | 32 | 32 passed, 0 failed |

commits.pr_title: [Refactor] Derive is_reasoning_end from the engine grammar
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose ### Context vLLM often needs to answer one question about a list of token ids: **is the model still inside a reasoning block?** Two things depend on the answer: - **Structured output.** When a request asks for JSON, the grammar must not be applied while the model is still thinking, or the model can never write its `` block. The engine core asks `is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)` once before generation, then checks each step. - **Streaming.** Before the first token, the frontend asks the same question about the prompt to decide whether to start parsing in reasoning mode or content mode. Both callers only have token ids. They have no text and have not fed anything into a parser. So `is_reasoning_end` has to be a plain function of the token ids. ### The problem: one grammar, three walkers The question "what ends reasoning?" is answered in three places. Two derive from the grammar. The third is maintained by hand, per model — and it is the one the structured-output gate reads at prompt time. ### The design: one table, one executor, two projections Every "what ends reasoning" fact now comes from the table. But the readers are not one machine: the frontend engine executes the table; the two id-only readers project it — and they read the same projected set. That shared node is the point of the drawing. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/parser/ tests/reasoning/ tests/tool_parsers/ ``` Beyond unit tests, the change was validated against real vLLM servers. ### Method `is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)` gates whether the guided-decoding bitmask applies from token 0 or is deferred. Both failure modes are silent (HTTP 200, normal `finish_reason`, nothing logged), so this was tested as an **A/B differential vs `main` (`c7e9816c6`)**: PR and `main` servers on separate GPUs, same requests at `temperature=0, seed=0` — any output difference is signal. Each pair was verified via `/proc//maps` to have loaded different trees, so "identical" can't be a harness artifact. Per model: plain chat / `json_schema` / tool calling, each × thinking on+off; after-tool-response turns; prior completed tool call + schema; `json_object`; forced `tool_choice`; streaming variants. Plus per-model probes: `tool_choice=required`, back-to-back tool calls, marker injection via user text, 5+ turn conversations, `continue_final_message` prefills, `structured_outputs` regex/choice/grammar, `include_reasoning=false`, `/v1/responses`. ### Results | Model | Parser | Pairs | Result | |---|---|---|---| | `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | gemma4 | 41 | byte-identical | | `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | gemma4 (E-series) | 49 | byte-identical | | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` | qwen3 | ~90 | identical on all `add_generation_prompt` paths | | `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` | qwen3 | 60 | byte-identical | | `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` | glm47 | 50 | byte-identical | | `mistralai/Magistral-Small-2509` | mistral (`special_token`) | 61 | byte-identical | | `gemma-4-E4B` via `/v1/responses` | gemma4 | 20 | byte-identical | | offline: kimi_k2 / glm47-off / deepseek_v32 / inkling / mistral(special_token,none) / nemotron_v3 / ling3 | — | 369 | 0 disagreements | Equivalence also confirmed mechanically: gemma4's derived `_reasoning_end_token_ids` = `{, <|tool_call>}` and its new `turn_boundary_tokens` reproduce the deleted override's branches exactly; `kimi_k2` derives `{, <|tool_calls_section_begin|>}`, matching its override term for term. `inkling`'s explicit `wait_for_reasoning=True` is load-bearing — the derived default would have made it constant `True`. `functools.cache` staleness ruled out by building configs in both orders. ### Bugs this PR fixes | Case | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | GLM-4.7, `` tail, thinking+schema | fenced block, missing required key, 5 extra keys (172 tok) | conformant JSON (20 tok) | | Qwen3-8B, 4 prefill shapes | free text / `location` instead of `city` | schema-valid | | seed_oss, mimo, thinking off | grammar never applied | applied | | Mistral-Small-3.2, thinking-off prefill | leading prose, violates schema | conformant | ### Reviewer notes * `extract_content_ids` still scans only the singular `_reasoning_end_token_id` while `is_reasoning_end` uses the derived set — they disagree on a ``-terminated sequence. Nothing pairs them today. * `<|tool_response>` in gemma4's new `turn_boundary_tokens` is inert — `grep -rn '"tool_responses"' vllm/` returns zero hits; `responses/utils.py:312-323` emits an ordinary `role: "tool"` message. `<|turn>` is live and load-bearing. * `minimax_m2`, `glm47_moe`, `kimi_k2`, `deepseek_v4` declare no `turn_boundary_tokens`, so the unbounded backward scan can latch onto a tool-start token in the system prompt's own format example (shown on minimax_m2: index 173/235). Latent only because those templates end the generation prompt with a reasoning marker; `continue_final_message` breaks that shield. Declaring boundaries, as this PR does for gemma4, would close it. * `seed_oss` requires #54264 (already on `main`), which adds `TURN_BOUNDARIES = frozenset(("", ""))`. Verified with this PR + #54264: boundaries resolve to `[0, 2]` and thinking-on + tools is unchanged from `main`. Rebasing onto a base older than #54264 would not be safe.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Honor `add_generation_prompt` in DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1 renderers
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust DeepSeek chat renderers always appended `<｜Assistant｜>` (and `<think>` / `</think>`) after a last user-like turn, even when `add_generation_prompt` is false. HF, Kimi K3, and Inkling already honor the flag.

Skip that suffix only when the user-like (or V4 trailing system / V4.1 mid-system) turn is the last **rendered** entry **and** `add_generation_prompt` is false. If an assistant message follows, the suffix is still written so the existing conversation can continue.

V3.2 uses `write_user_like_suffix`. V4 and V4.1 share `write_assistant_transition` and inspect the next rendered entry, not the raw message index, because V4 merges trailing tool results into the current user block.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `add_generation_prompt deepseek rust`.

- #46257 is the **Python** DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer (`add_generation_prompt` / `continue_final_message`), not these Rust renderers.

## Test Plan

```
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-chat deepseek_v32
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-chat deepseek_v4
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-chat deepseek_v41
```

Result: **19** V3.2 unit tests plus V4/V4.1 unit tests, and `roundtrip_deepseek_v32`, `roundtrip_deepseek_v4`, `roundtrip_deepseek_v41`.

New cases:

- last user + default `add_generation_prompt` → prompt ends with `<｜Assistant｜><think>`
- last user + `NoGenerationPrompt` → prompt ends at user text (no `<｜Assistant｜>`)
- user then assistant + `NoGenerationPrompt` → suffix still present before assistant content

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSpark] Collapse DeepSeek-V4.1 draft states before SP all-gather
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Under sequence parallelism, the DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark draft gathers BF16 `[T_local, 4, H]` residual streams and FP32 `[T_local, 4]` pre-mix coefficients before collapsing them into `[T, H]`. The draft returns only the collapsed pre-norm head states; it does not export a full-HC MTP buffer at this boundary.

Collapse each token's streams locally, then gather only `[T_local, H]` and trim SP padding. This reduces the hidden-state gather payload by 4x for `hc_mult=4` and removes the pre-mix gather, reducing this tail from two collectives to one. The target model already follows this ordering when it does not need to export full HC states. Normalization remains in `compute_logits`.

This is a communication optimization, not an output-correctness fix. SP currently requires PP=1, EP enabled, TP>1, and either a MegaMoE backend or DP>1.

### Duplicate-work check

No existing issue was identified for this optimization; issue-number duplicate checks are not applicable. Open-PR searches covered `dspark collapse`, `DeepSeek sequence parallel`, `"hc_collapse_triton"`, and `"dspark" "gather" in:title`. No matching fix was found. Reviewed related PRs: #50658 projects Kimi-K3 target auxiliary states; #56438 handles V4.1 pipeline/SP stage boundaries; #51244 adds V4 kernel fusions; #56513 changes the ROCm delayed mHC projection. None applies this NVIDIA V4.1 draft-tail reorder.

## Test Plan

- Extend the existing mHC kernel suite with a single-GPU dummy test comparing concatenate-then-collapse against collapse-each-shard-then-concatenate. Cover TP4/TP8, T=1/7/32, padding, and ranks with no valid tokens. Require exact BF16 equality (`atol=0, rtol=0`).
- Run the existing collapse correctness, custom-op/compile, and draft-head tests.
- Use a standalone measurement harness (not included in the PR diff) to benchmark the exact tail (`mhc_post_tilelang` + collapse + production `sp_all_gather`) before and after, using random tensors and no model weights. Check eager and captured outputs bitwise before timing. Include an NCCL-only control.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'hc_collapse or v41_dspark_head' -v

# Retrieve the standalone harness from the measurement commit.
git show 16dc4cc4d05f86cf8fd0c7413e327395337d2371:benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dspark_sp_collapse.py \
  > /tmp/benchmark_dspark_sp_collapse.py

.venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 \
  /tmp/benchmark_dspark_sp_collapse.py

.venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 \
  /tmp/benchmark_dspark_sp_collapse.py --nccl-only

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py \
  tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py

git diff --check
```

## Test Result

- **25 passed**, 177 deselected. Includes all six new single-GPU shard-order cases; 14 existing Torch deprecation warnings.
- TP4: all six shapes passed bitwise checks in eager execution and CUDA graph replay, for both default SP dispatch and NCCL-only. Repeated the default-dispatch run with the same result.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and whitespace check passed.
- Full-model evaluation and end-to-end serving benchmarks were not run. Validation is limited to tail-output equivalence and the scoped microbenchmark; no acceptance-rate, model-quality, or serving-throughput claim is made.

### Scoped tail performance

One node, 4x NVIDIA GB200 connected by NV18 links. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2, NCCL 2.29.7, Triton 3.7.1, TileLang 0.1.12, FlashInfer 0.6.18. BF16 streams/output, FP32 mixes, H=5120, hc_mult=4. Measurement commit: `16dc4cc4d05f86cf8fd0c7413e327395337d2371` (the standalone benchmark was subsequently removed from the PR; implementation and tests are unchanged), based on `00972dfd72988942138a7a6089eaee08580210b8`.

CUDA graph internal events exclude CPU launch gaps. Each measurement flushes 128 MiB of L2 and uses a device-side all-reduce rendezvous before replay, outside the timed interval. Four pointer-distinct workspaces, 20 warmup replays, 50 samples per variant, alternating A/B order. Report the median of each sample's slowest rank. Compilation, allocation and input generation are outside timing; all production gather staging/copies remain inside. The benchmark also reports logical receive bytes per rank and payload/time; this is not a measurement of physical link bandwidth.

All times below are microseconds for the entire tail. Default-dispatch figures are from the repeat run.

| Global T | Local padded T | Default before | Default after | Speedup | NCCL before | NCCL after | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 24.61 | 18.88 | 1.30x | 42.78 | 31.68 | 1.35x |
| 7 | 2 | 26.82 | 18.94 | 1.42x | 42.82 | 31.81 | 1.35x |
| 32 | 8 | 43.14 | 19.60 | 2.20x | 45.50 | 32.91 | 1.38x |
| 128 | 32 | 108.69 | 20.78 | 5.23x | 62.38 | 35.81 | 1.74x |
| 512 | 128 | 163.89 | 28.80 | 5.69x | 96.96 | 52.93 | 1.83x |
| 2048 | 512 | 168.43 | 88.14 | 1.91x | 180.82 | 90.94 | 1.99x |

The first default-dispatch run measured 1.29x/1.40x/2.10x/5.13x/5.76x/1.88x for the same ascending token counts. These are microbenchmark results, not end-to-end speedups.

Backend selection is part of the measured production wrapper: at T<=128, both versions' state gathers use MNNVL Lamport; at T=512, the original full-state gather falls back while the smaller collapsed gather still uses MNNVL; at T=2048, both state gathers fall back. The original pre-mix gather uses MNNVL throughout. The NCCL-only control disables custom gathers. Real distributed measurements cover TP4; TP8 is covered by single-GPU sharding-equivalence tests only.

## Purpose

Raise parallelism on the one V1 misc successor job whose tests still exceed a 20-minute test budget (image/dependency setup excluded):

Simulated per-shard job time (kv shard + ec shard, minutes):

| N | slowest (median weights) | slowest (worst-observed weights) | empty shards |

| 2 | 19.7 | 24.8 | 0 |
| 3 | 13.5 | 17.3 | 0 |
| **4** | **10.9** | **13.8** | 0 |
| 5 | 11.5 | 13.9 | 0 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Handle aborted requests in beam search
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Aborting an inner beam-search request before it generates a token can return `logprobs=[]`. Both the online and offline paths only check for `None` before reading `logprobs[0]`, so this raises `IndexError`. With `/pause?mode=abort`, a running `/v1/completions` request returns HTTP 500.

Stop the affected search when an inner request reports `finish_reason="abort"`. Keep the prefixes, logprobs, and scores from the last completed beam step, and mark active beams as aborted. This also prevents surviving siblings from submitting another step to the paused engine. Other prompts in an offline batch continue.

Also handle scoring a preserved prefix containing only an EOS prompt token, which would otherwise divide by zero.

## Test Plan

Add online and offline regressions for aborts before the first token and after a beam expansion, covering `None`, empty, and nonempty terminal logprobs. Include mixed aborted/normal children, an EOS-only prompt, and an independent offline prompt.

Run the focused CPU cases and the existing candidate-indexing and decoding tests, with the repository's parent conftest excluded:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/samplers \
  tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py \
  -k 'abort_returns_partial_outputs or extra_logprob or respects_skip_special_tokens' \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/online.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/offline.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/utils.py \
  tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py \
  tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix: all 18 new regression cases fail; the existing candidate-indexing test passes.
- After the fix: **21 passed** on macOS with CPU dependencies, rechecked after rebasing on September 15, 2026. This includes the two upstream `skip_special_tokens` cases.
- All applicable pre-commit checks and the separate mypy 3.12 check passed.

Also ran before/after model smoke tests on September 10, 2026, on a single A10 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`:

- Online: start a beam-search request through `/v1/completions`, then call `/pause?mode=abort` with server dev mode enabled. Before the fix, all three attempts return HTTP 500 with `list index out of range`. After the fix, all three return HTTP 200 with eight choices marked `abort`, preserving generated prefixes and logprobs. Each request finishes while the engine is still paused.
- Offline: call `LLM.beam_search` and use the engine's pause utility to abort before the second beam step. The engine returns a mix of normal and aborted children, with empty logprobs on the aborted ones. Before the fix, this raises `IndexError`. After the fix, it returns eight beams, each retaining the first generated token and marked `abort`, without submitting a third step.
- Normal online and offline control generations match the baseline, including after pause/resume.

Checked open, closed, and merged beam-search PRs on September 10, 2026; no equivalent abort-handling fix was found. The candidate-indexing fix in [#47126](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47126) leaves this abort path unchanged.

AI assistance: Codex helped with the investigation, implementation, and tests.

commits.pr_title: [Build] Move DeepGEMM pin to the vLLM fork and update the Mega MoE call convention
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Repoint the DeepGEMM pin from `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` `nv_dev` (2.6.1, `8b1392b`) to `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` at [`9a86ae2b`](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/9a86ae2b78991f1c8e6e95945a591e1ca3b19ce7) (2.8.0), and update the Mega MoE call convention that comes with it.

`9a86ae2b` is the tip of the fork's `dev` branch: the upstream 26/09 public release plus five fork-only commits — the SM120 (consumer Blackwell) port and the SM90 paged-MQA `kv_block=32`/`next_n=4` port that we were pinning `nv_dev` for, a Mega MoE task-info slot-release fix, configurable SwiGLU alpha/beta, and SiTU for FP8/FP4 Mega MoE. Staying on `nv_dev` means we cannot pick up the 2.8.0 release line without losing SM120 and SM90 paged-MQA coverage.

Both arch ports matter here. The 2.8.0 release line dropped the SM90 2-CTA KV multicast, which `next_n=4` and `kv_block=32` depended on — that support had only ever lived on `nv_dev`. An earlier revision of this PR therefore had to degrade H100: MTP=3 decode fell back to the flattened path, and the kpool indexer had to align to 64-entry pages. `vllm-project/DeepGEMM#7` ports that SM90 support forward instead, so this PR needs **no** vLLM-side SM90 changes — `native_next_n_supported`, `_paged_mqa_logits_schedule_slots` and the kpool page alignment are all untouched.

### Mega MoE call convention

2.8.0 replaces the SiTU-specific optional pair with a generic one on `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (and adds it to `bf16_mega_moe`):

| 2.6.1 | 2.8.0 | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `situ_beta: float \| None = None` | `activation_alpha: float = 1.0` | SiTU gate tanh scale |
| `situ_linear_beta: float \| None = None` | `activation_beta: float = 0.0` | SiTU linear/up tanh scale; `0.0` leaves the up branch unchanged |

Under `swiglu` the same two floats now parameterize `gate * sigmoid(alpha * gate) * (up + beta)`, and the defaults `1.0` / `0.0` are exactly the previous behavior — so the DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 call sites need no change. Kimi K3 is the only site in the tree that passed the SiTU parameters through to DeepGEMM, so it is the only call site updated here.

Two related semantics, both no-ops for us in practice:

- `activation_beta` may now be `0` (meaning "no tanh on the up branch", matching an unset `situ_linear_beta` in FlashInfer). 2.6.1 asserted `situ_linear_beta > 0`.
- `activation_clamp` is now silently ignored under SiTU rather than asserted-unset. Kimi K3 already passes `None`.

Note that vLLM's own `activation_situ_beta` / `activation_situ_linear_beta` config names (`FusedMoEConfig` and the TRT-LLM / CuteDSL / AITER backends) are deliberately left alone; only the mapping at the DeepGEMM call boundary changes.

### Build plumbing

2.8.0 drops the `third-party/fmt` submodule in favor of `third-party/deep_jit`, so this updates `GIT_SUBMODULES`, the `_C` include path in `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py`, and the header glob that retriggers the `_C` rebuild. `docker/Dockerfile` gains `elfutils-devel`, matching #56266 / #56255.

### Second commit: masked grouped FP8 GEMM

Verification turned up a real breakage that the pin bump would otherwise have
shipped: 2.8.0 also drops the legacy `fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked` Python
alias. `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` resolved it via `getattr(..., None)`, so it
silently became `None` and every call raised *"DeepGEMM backend is unavailable"*,
taking out `BatchedDeepGemmExperts`. The second commit looks up the canonical
`m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_masked` with the legacy spelling as a fallback. Both
names alias the same `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_masked` binding, whose C++
signature and pybind defaults are byte-identical across 2.6.1 and 2.8.0.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR moves the pin to the vLLM fork. The closest neighbors are #56266 (Mega-Gate) and #56255 (Mega-mHC), which both pin `deepseek-ai@39d8c4ca` and carry the same `fmt` → `deep_jit` plumbing and the same `elfutils-devel` hunk.

That base is the same 26/09 release this PR sits on; what neither can reach from `deepseek-ai/main` is the fork's four extra commits, in particular SM120 and SiTU. So the build-plumbing hunks in this PR do overlap with those two, and whichever lands first leaves the others a trivial rebase — that overlap is stated here rather than papered over. The activation-parameter rename and the Kimi K3 call site are unique to this PR.

One caveat on `elfutils-devel`: I could not find any `libelf` consumer in DeepGEMM 2.8.0 or in DeepJIT (both are header-only, and `<format>` is what replaced fmt). It is included here to match the sibling PRs; if a reviewer knows it is unnecessary, it should be dropped from all three.

## Test plan

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1, driver 580.126.09, torch 2.13.0+cu130.

**Build.** `cmake --preset release` fetches `vllm-project/DeepGEMM@e49b29bb` with
the `deep_jit` submodule (no `fmt`), and `--target _deep_gemm_C` builds `_C`
clean. The vendored package then imports as 2.8.0 and exposes the new
`activation_alpha`/`activation_beta` signature. `_C` links without `libelf`,
which is why I flagged the `elfutils-devel` hunk above.

**SiTU convention (the load-bearing part of this PR).** Single-rank numerical
check of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe(activation='situ')` against a PyTorch reference
implementing `alpha*tanh(gate/alpha)*sigmoid(gate) * beta*tanh(up/beta)`, at
Kimi K3's own config values (`activation_situ_beta=4.0`,
`activation_situ_linear_beta=25.0`):

| run | `calc_diff` vs reference |
| --- | --- |
| `activation_alpha=4.0, activation_beta=25.0` | **3.56e-04** |
| alpha/beta swapped (control) | 1.36e-01 |

3.56e-04 is the quantization error floor — dequantizing the FP8 activations
alone gives 3.60e-04. The swapped control is ~380x worse, so a reversed
assignment would have been caught rather than passing silently.

**Unit tests.**

```
tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py
tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py
tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
tests/models/glm5next/                              -> 81 passed

tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py ................ 9 passed, 3 skipped
tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py  passed
```

`test_batched_deepgemm.py` is the regression test for the second commit: with
that commit reverted it fails immediately with the `RuntimeError` above; with it,
32 pass.

Note my hardware is SM100, so none of this exercises the SM90 paths. The H100
`nvidia-h100-deepgemm-kernels` job is the real gate there — it is what caught the
2.8.0 SM90 regression on an earlier revision of this PR, before the fork ported
the SM90 support forward.

**Pre-existing failure, not from this PR.**
`tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py::test_w8a8_block_fp8_deep_gemm_matmul`
fails on my machine with `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (719)` out of
`cuLaunchKernelEx`, and the sticky context error cascades into ~254 downstream
errors in the same pytest process. This is **not** caused by the bump: I built
the old 2.6.1 pin's `_C` side by side and swapped it in, and the identical 719
reproduces there (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d` on 2.6.1, `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d` on
2.8.0). Also ruled out: stale JIT cache, PDL, GEMM shape, and target arch (both
compile `sm_100f`; device is cc 10.0). Grouped DeepGEMM paths are unaffected and
pass. I believe this is local to my setup, but I could not get a clean signal on
that suite either way, so I am flagging it rather than reporting it green.

**Model eval.** Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, `hidden_act=situ`, mxfp4
experts) GSM8K with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel
--tensor-parallel-size 4`, which is the only path that exercises the changed
call site end to end. The engine log confirms `moe_backend='deep_gemm_mega_moe'` with EP enabled, so
the changed call site is genuinely on the path.

Because a single number proves little against a 75%-pruned checkpoint, I ran an
A/B on the same build and identical server config, varying only the MoE backend:

| backend, 500 questions, 5-shot | GSM8K | invalid rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deep_gemm_mega_moe` (SiTU, the changed call site) | 0.3160 | 0.008 |
| `auto` (non-MegaMoE baseline) | 0.3100 | 0.006 |

The two are 0.006 apart against a ~2.1% 1-sigma at n=500, i.e. statistically
indistinguishable — the SiTU MegaMoE path matches the non-MegaMoE baseline
end to end. The MegaMoE arm was also measured at 0.3080 on the previous pin
(`e49b29bb`, before the SM90 port), so run-to-run spread on this setup is
around 0.8pp, which is itself larger than the gap being tested.

For transparency on the absolute level: both sit below this checkpoint's
reference threshold of 0.33 (the repo's own config for it pairs it with dspark
speculative decoding, fp8 KV cache and the flashinfer MLA prefill, all of which
I dropped to isolate the MoE path). The suite reports these as passing only
because its assertion is `measured >= threshold - 0.08`. The A/B, not the
threshold, is what supports the claim here.

**Second model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, TP4 on GB200, to cover a DSA model whose
indexer drives `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` / `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` —
a different DeepGEMM surface from Kimi K3's MegaMoE. Both runs are from this
branch with a clean working tree, so both reproduce from the PR as submitted.

| eval | result | reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, n=1319 | flexible-extract **0.9303** / strict-match **0.9303** | 0.9265 / 0.9257 on the same recipe before this change |
| GPQA-Diamond, 4 epochs, thinking, n=792 | exact_match **0.9116**, 0 request errors | no prior measurement |

GSM8K is the load-bearing one: it has a recorded pre-change baseline on this
exact recipe and lands slightly above it, so the pin bump shows no DSv4.1
regression. GPQA-Diamond had no prior DSv4.1 run to compare against, so it is a
health check — a hard reasoning eval completing with zero request errors — not a
regression test. Sampling followed the DeepSeek V4 reference recipe (temperature
1.0, top_p 0.95, `max_tokens` 57344, concurrency 128).

## What

Fix an engine-startup crash when a sparse-MLA model captures decode batches with **piecewise** cudagraphs (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash, a hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA model):

```log
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Full startup traceback (4x GB300, TP4, `load_format=dummy`; identical with real weights, the capture path does not read weights):

```log
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 988, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 920, in profile_cudagraph_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 456, in capture
File "vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 206, in add_eager
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 1483, in unified_mla_attention_with_output
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py", line 736, in _convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 95, in convert_logical_to_physical_topk
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py", line 133, in _convert_once
    self.side_stream.wait_event(self.logical_topk_ready)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

## Root cause

`SparseMLAIndexGroup` overlaps the logical→physical topk conversion with the compute stream via the `logical_topk_ready` event: the indexer records it on the compute stream after computing topk, and `_convert_once` waits on it on the side stream.

In piecewise cudagraph mode the indexer runs **inside a captured graph segment**, while the consumer runs in the following **eager break** (`unified_mla_attention_with_output` is an `@eager_break_during_capture` point, executed by `add_eager()` after the segment's `capture_end()`). An event recorded during stream capture is graph-local; waiting on it eagerly is `cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

Minimal reproduction of the exact pattern (no vLLM involved):

```python
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    ev.record(torch.cuda.current_stream())   # inside capture
side.wait_event(ev)                          # eager, after capture -> invalid argument
```

Why only some models: FULL cudagraph capture (non-hybrid sparse MLA, e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2 decode) records and waits in-graph, which is legal; prefill-sized batches take the workspace-overflow branch of `_convert_once`, which never touches the event. Hybrid models like GLM-5.3-Flash capture decode batches piecewise and hit the crash during `profile_cudagraph_memory`.

## Fix

In piecewise mode, skip the event entirely: `set_logical_topk_ready` does not record (a record inside a capture segment would be graph-local and unusable anyway), and `_convert_once` orders the side stream with `wait_stream(compute_stream)` — identical to the existing `has_indexer=False` path, and correct because the convert is always invoked after the indexer on the same compute stream. FULL/eager modes keep the fine-grained event. The same guard is applied to the HiSparse copy stream. Adds `in_piecewise_cudagraph()` to `forward_context.py`.

## Tests

- New regression test (record inside captured segment + convert in eager break under `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`); fails pre-fix at `index_group.py:133` with the production error, passes post-fix:

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k piecewise_capture`

- Sparse MLA subset (convert / index_group / piecewise / hisparse): 47 passed

  `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "convert or index_group or piecewise or hisparse"`

- E2E on 4x GB300, GLM-5.3-Flash real weights, TP4: engine starts with cudagraphs enabled (crashed at startup before), generation works.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4x GB300 (this branch, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, no speculative decoding): **91.8%** accuracy (invalid rate 0.0%).

## Notes

- Bisect: the crash starts with #53781, which introduced the side-stream + `logical_topk_ready` event for the topk conversion (before it, the convert ran on the compute stream with no event). Verified empirically: its parent commit starts cleanly, it crashes at engine startup. Purely informational for locating the change — the piecewise interaction was easy to miss.
- Duplicate check: no open PR covers this crash; #54851 is a different piecewise-mode issue (KV-cache writes baked into captured graphs for DSA models on multi-node TP).
- AI assistance: developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); all changes reviewed and tested by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Clarify ITL vs TPOT Prometheus metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Resolves #55276. The [Metrics design documentation](docs/design/metrics.md) incorrectly labeled `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds` as "Time Per Output Token (TPOT)". This is misleading because vLLM exposes two distinct metrics:

- `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds` - one sample per decode output event (the wall-clock gap between consecutive NEW_TOKENS` events); this is ITL.
- `vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds` - recorded once per finished  request as `decode_time / (num_generation_tokens - 1)`; this is TPOT.

The two differ under speculative decoding (one output bundles multiple tokens) and when mean ITL and mean per-request TPOT use differing aggregation weights. This PR corrects the docs and adds a TPOT panel to the reference Grafana dashboard.

Changes:
- `docs/design/metrics.md`: fix the incorrect TPOT label on  `inter_token_latency_seconds`, add `request_time_per_output_token_seconds`  to the metric list, and add a note that the latter is the metric matching
  `vllm bench serve` per-request TPOT.
- `examples/observability/prometheus_grafana/grafana.json`: update the ITL  panel description and add a new "Time Per Output Token (TPOT)" panel  (P50/P90/P95/P99/Mean) using `request_time_per_output_token_seconds`.

This is a documentation-only change; no runtime code was modified.

## Test Plan

- N/A (documentation + Grafana dashboard JSON change only).
- `python -c "import json; json.load(open('examples/observability/prometheus_grafana/grafana.json'))"` validated the dashboard JSON.

## Test Result

Grafana dashboard JSON parses successfully. No model evaluation required because this change does not affect output, accuracy, or serving.

Note: Since this is a docs-only change (no runtime code), no model evals are run per the AGENTS.md guidance that evals apply to model-affecting changes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Keep transient checkpoints out of prefix-cache eviction
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Keep transient KDA/Mamba prefill checkpoints out of the ordinary prefix-cache eviction set when sparse retention is explicitly active.

This change targets Kimi-K3's hybrid attention path.

## Problem

FlashKDA creates internal checkpoints so the current prefill can continue from a recurrent-state boundary without an additional scheduling step. A checkpoint in the middle of a prompt is useful to the current request, but it is not necessarily a reusable shared-prefix boundary.

Before this change, such a checkpoint could be re-keyed and registered as a normal prefix-cache block. It then participated in the same GPU LRU eviction pool as reusable hot prefixes:

```text
middle checkpoint -> hash -> prefix-cache LRU -> evicts hot prefix
                                             -> later local hit becomes a miss
                                             -> extra load or prefill work
```

Before/after cache lifecycle:

```text
Before:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint
      |        |
      |        +--> hash + ordinary LRU
      |                     |
      |                     +--> competes with hot prefix
      |                                  |
      |                                  +--> local prefix miss

After:

  KDA prefill
      |
      +--> temporary checkpoint ------------------> current request can use it
      |                                              |
      |                                              +--> no ordinary LRU entry
      |
      +--> shared-prefix-boundary checkpoint ------> reusable prefix cache
                                                     |
                                                     +--> may be retained/shared
```

This is particularly problematic when `prefix_cache_retention_interval == 0`: intermediate checkpoints are not intended to be retained as dense semantic checkpoints, but their temporary hash could still make them eviction candidates.

## Fix

Pass the active retention interval into checkpoint publication. When sparse retention is active and the checkpoint is neither at the end of the prompt nor at the shared-prefix boundary, treat it as request-local state:

```text
middle checkpoint -> current request may use it
                  -> temporary hash is removed
                  -> no ordinary prefix-cache LRU entry
                  -> reusable hot prefixes remain protected
```

Prompt-end and shared-prefix-boundary checkpoints retain the existing publication behavior. This change does not disable KDA checkpoint computation or change the state written by FlashKDA.

## Performance

On a representative B200 Kimi-K3 hybrid workload using TP8/PP2/direct DCP8, the isolated production-style comparison was:

| Configuration | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: |
| Checkpoint disabled (diagnostic baseline) | 1013.00 tokens/s |
| Checkpoint enabled with transient-checkpoint retention fix | 1091.80 tokens/s |

The fixed configuration improved throughput by 7.78% over the checkpoint-disabled diagnostic baseline while retaining the internal checkpoint feature. A separate run with the GEMM-AR option disabled measured 1108.89 tokens/s; that result is included only as context and is not an isolated measurement of this patch.

These measurements are workload-specific and are not used as a claim that this small cache-lifecycle change explains every difference between software stacks. The primary regression signal is the cache-manager reproduction: temporary checkpoint publication changes which blocks compete in the local prefix-cache eviction pool.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- PR #55760 changes the default sparse/dense retention policy for Mamba + EAGLE; this change keeps the explicit sparse-retention behavior but fixes transient checkpoint publication.
- PR #56615 fixes MooncakeStore boundary pairing between Mamba/KDA and attention KV; this change is limited to local prefix-cache block retention.
- PR #56525 guards cache hits until the writing scheduler step is committed; this change addresses eviction eligibility, not write visibility.
- PR #52527 adds observability for sparse-retention misses; this change modifies the cache lifecycle.

## Validation

Focused prefix-cache tests should be run with:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
```

The change is intentionally small and preserves the current-request checkpoint path. Model-scale performance validation is still required on a representative hybrid KDA workload.

This change was prepared with AI assistance; the author should review the complete diff and test results before merging.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix stale HPC QK-norm weights after weight refit
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`HpcRopeNorm` kept float32 mirror Parameters (`qnorm_weight` / `knorm_weight`) of the
`q_norm` / `k_norm` weights. They were filled by `process_weights_after_loading()`, and that
hook was dispatched **only** by the generic `HpcModule` loop in
`model_executor/model_loader/utils.py`, which runs at cold start.

No reload path reaches that loop:

| path | dispatcher | reaches the HPC loop? |
|---|---|---|
| `base_loader.load_model` | `utils.process_weights_after_loading` | yes (cold start only) |
| `weight_cache/ipc_loader` | same | yes (cold start only) |
| `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` | `initialize/finalize_layerwise_reload` | **no** |
| NCCL / IPC / sharded-RDT weight transfer | same | **no** |
| `wake_up` after sleep | CuMemAllocator restore | **no** |

`layerwise.py` only dispatches `process_weights_after_loading` for layers carrying a
`QuantizeMethodBase` and for deferred attention layers. `HpcRopeNorm` is neither, so after an
RL weight refit the fused kernel consumed **pre-refit** QK-norm weights — silently, with no
error and no warning.

### Fix

Build `q_norm` / `k_norm` in float32 when the HPC path is active, and have the kernel read
them directly. No derived copy means nothing to refresh, on any load path. The checkpoint is
untouched (still bf16) — `default_weight_loader` casts on `param.data.copy_()`.

### Cleanup bundled in (not a fix)

`HpcIHCPre` / `HpcIHCHead` bound owner weight *aliases* in the same hook. Those aliases do
survive refits (verified empirically, see Test Result), so their forwards now read the owner
attributes directly purely to remove the last reason for the hook to exist. With no
`HpcModule` needing it, the three overrides, the base no-op and the loader loop are deleted
(4 `process_weights_after_loading` mounting points → 3).

The two failure modes are different and it matters:

| | what was cached | after a refit |
|---|---|---|
| `HpcIHCPre` / `HpcIHCHead` | an **alias** to the owner's Parameter | pointer unchanged, alias still valid |
| `HpcRopeNorm` | an independent `copy_().float()` **duplicate** | nobody refreshes it → stale values |

An alias follows its owner because layerwise reload's `_copy_and_restore_kernel_tensors`
copies in place and `_place_kernel_tensors` re-registers the original Parameter objects.
A duplicate does not.

## Test Plan

```bash
# lint (all hooks, changed files)
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD)

# unit
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -v -m "not slow_test"
```

New test `test_hpc_rope_norm_kernel_sees_refit_norm_weights` drives the production
`_forward_impl` with a recording `hpc` stub and asserts the kernel receives the refit Q **and**
K weights, float32, same storage.

End-to-end on GB200 (sm100) with Tencent **hpc-ops** built from source, HY4
(`HYV4ForCausalLM`, `enable_ihc: true`, `hc_mult: 4`, `hidden_size: 6144`), three arms —
`base`, `base2` (same code as `base`, to establish the run-to-run noise floor), `pr` — plus a
deliberately perturbed arm as a positive control.

## Test Result

**Unit** — `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -m "not slow_test"`, run inside
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (aarch64, GB200):

| | result |
|---|---|
| without this PR | 27 passed, 2 failed |
| with this PR | **28 passed, 1 failed** |

`test_hpc_rope_norm_kernel_sees_refit_norm_weights` **FAILS without the change and PASSES with
it** — it is the new test, and it does catch the bug.

The one remaining failure, `test_kv_scale_reload`, fails identically with and without the
change; it is pre-existing in that image and unrelated.

Applying only this PR's `utils.py` deletion (the `HpcModule` loop + its import) on top of an
otherwise untouched tree gives byte-identical results to not applying it, confirming the
removed mounting point is inert for every non-HPC path.

**Lint** — `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all hooks pass. (mypy initially flagged
`rope_norm.py:398-399 Item "None" of "Any | None" has no attribute "weight"` — the same latent
crash the removed `fallback_qnorm is not None` guard used to prevent. Fixed by validating the
invariant in `__init__` with an explicit `ValueError` and narrowing at the use site.)

**End-to-end, HY4 on GB200 / sm100** — the HPC gate fires: `HpcIHCPre: 8`, `HpcIHCPost: 8`,
`HpcIHCHead: 1`, `gated_mla_layers: 4`, identical across arms, so the changed code really is
executed.

`process_weights_after_loading` mounting points, read off the live model:

```
base: ['HpcIHCHead', 'HpcIHCPre', 'MLAAttention', 'UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod']
pr:   [                           'MLAAttention', 'UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod']
```

Exactly the two HPC hooks are removed; the other mounting points are untouched.

Output equivalence — greedy, fixed prompts, token ids compared one by one:

| | vs base |
|---|---|
| pr (cudagraph) | **8/8 identical** |
| pr (eager) | **8/8 identical** |
| base2 (same code, control) | 8/8 identical |
| **positive control** (`hc_fn.weight * 1.01` on the changed line) | **6/8 diverge**, first at token 56 |

The positive control is what makes the 8/8 meaningful: the same test does detect a
perturbation on the very line this PR touches.

Throughput, batch 256 × 512 output tokens, 7 reps, median:

| mode | pr vs base | same-code noise floor (base2) |
|---|---|---|
| cudagraph | +0.16% | +0.15% |
| eager (run 1) | +1.21% | +0.05% |
| eager (run 2) | +2.91% | **+2.47%** |

In eager run 2 the *same code* (`base2`) moved +2.47%, so the apparent gain tracks arm
ordering (warm-up), not the change. No measurable difference in either mode, which matches the
mechanism — a handful of extra attribute lookups per forward.

Refit-alias validity, `reload_weights` on the `base` arm (the claim that the iHC cleanup is
not a fix):

```
modules holding a cached alias: 9  (8x HpcIHCPre + 1x HpcIHCHead)
alias still points at the live weight after reload: 9 / 9
sample pointer before -> after: 26843826176 -> 26843826176   (unchanged)
generation identical after reload: 6 / 6
```

Confirms the alias half is genuinely cleanup.

**GSM8K on the full 78-layer model** — the 4-layer slice I first used has no
discriminating power (every arm, including a deliberately sabotaged one, scores 0.000 with
`invalid_rate=0.985`), so I pulled the full `tencent/Hy4-preview` (131 shards, 1.5 TB bf16) and
re-ran on 4 nodes / 16 GPUs, TP=4 x PP=4 with expert parallelism, via
`distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`:

| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_modules` | `HpcIHCPre: 156, HpcIHCPost: 156, HpcIHCHead: 1` | identical |
| `gated_mla_layers` | 78 | identical |
| greedy output, 8 prompts | — | **8/8 token-identical** |
| **GSM8K accuracy (500 q, 5-shot)** | **0.5660** | **0.5660** |
| GSM8K invalid_rate | 0.0120 | 0.0120 |

156 = 78 layers x 2 iHC boundaries per layer, so the changed path is exercised on every layer.
`invalid_rate` drops from 0.985 on the slice to 0.012 here, i.e. the model is actually
answering and the score is meaningful. Accuracy is identical between the arms.

(0.566 is the raw-completion score without a chat template; it is used only for the A/B
comparison, not as a claim about the model's ceiling.)

### Not verified

**sm90 + HY3 + `HPC_ATTN` refit.** `HpcAttentionBackend.supports_compute_capability` is
`capability == DeviceCapability(9, 0)`, so the actual fix (`HpcRopeNorm`, `hy_v3.py`) cannot be
exercised on sm100 at all — my cluster is GB200 only. What I verified end-to-end is the iHC
cleanup half plus the mounting-point removal. I'd appreciate the Tencent hpc-ops authors (or
anyone with H100/H800) running an sm90 refit-consistency check; the script must **fail on
`main`**, otherwise it isn't exercising the bug.

### Reproducing the hpc-ops build

hpc-ops ships no wheel (no GitHub release, nothing on PyPI), and building it inside
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` needs three environment fixes unrelated to this PR:

1. PyPI is throttled on some clusters — prefetch build deps and install with `--no-index`.
2. The image has no `git`, and `hpc-ops/setup.py:get_version()` shells out to it for a short hash.
3. CUDA headers come from the `nvidia-*-cu13` wheels, so `cusparse.h` is not under
   `/usr/local/cuda/include`; torch's `ATen/cuda/CUDAContextLight.h` fails to include it.
   `export CPATH=<site-packages>/nvidia/cu13/include`.

## Known limitation

Sharded-state artifacts saved by an older build contain the retired
`hpc_rope_norm.qnorm_weight` / `knorm_weight` keys; `ShardedStateLoader` indexes `state_dict`
by checkpoint key and raises `KeyError`. Regenerate the artifact.

Worth noting this swaps the direction of an existing incompatibility rather than introducing
one: on `main`, loading a sharded artifact saved *without* HPC into an HPC-enabled build
already fails, because those two keys stay in `state_dict` and hit
`raise ValueError(f"Missing keys {tuple(state_dict)} in loaded state!")`. I chose not to touch
the shared loader from an HPC PR — happy to add a narrow tolerance here or as a prerequisite PR
if maintainers prefer.

## Follow-ups deliberately left out of this PR

- `HpcRopeNorm.__init__` could also reject a non-float32 `fallback_qnorm.weight`. The fp32
  contract now lives with the caller (`hy_v3.py`), and `hy_v3` is the only in-tree caller, but
  nothing checks it for the next model that wires up `HPC_ATTN`.
- After this PR nothing does `isinstance(x, HpcModule)` anymore, and the base class is reduced
  to `support()` returning `True` plus a `pass` `forward()` — both overridden by every
  subclass. It is arguably dead and could be dropped.

---

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses HPC QK-norm staleness across weight reload
(searched `vllm-project/vllm` for `HpcRopeNorm`, `hpc qk norm refit`,
`process_weights_after_loading refit`; the only nearby open PR, #47443, changes HPC attention
decode split-K selection). RFC #54477 is the umbrella for selective weight reload in RL.

AI assistance was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed by me, and I ran the
lint, unit and end-to-end runs reported above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix multiple handles xfer race
commits.pr_body:
A request can own multiple in-flight NIXL transfer handles (one per remote TP rank under heterogeneous TP). 
On `main`, the first handle to reach `ERR` immediately invalidates the request's blocks and reports the failure to the scheduler, while the sibling handles may still be posting RDMA writes into those same blocks. 
Posted transfers cannot be aborted, so once the scheduler reassigns the blocks, the in-flight writes corrupt whichever request owns them next.

**This PR fixes this race** by deferring NIXL receive-failure reporting and block invalidation until all transfers for the request have stopped, preventing in-flight RDMA writes from corrupting reused KV blocks.

Some cascading changes to keep purpose of data structures clear:
- background threads use the existing `_failed_recv_reqs` Q to report failures
- main engine thread failures are reported on  `_recv_failures` set to minimize overhead
- `_failed_recv_reqs` Q failures are addressed in `get_finished`; `_pop_done_transfers` also returns current poll failures, so we can track them and check whether all handles have been processed (or we delay, *bulk of this PR*)

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][MoE] DeepEP v2: async finalize to overlap shared experts with combine
commits.pr_body:
> **Status (2026-08-31):** reviewer feedback addressed — overlap is now **default-on** (`VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=1`, capability-gated fallback, env is a kill-switch), rebased clean onto current main (no conflicts). **Blocked only on a `ready` label** so Buildkite can run — the full suite has never executed on this fork PR. Contract tests included; EP8 A/B in comments.

---

FIX #52744

### What

`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the ElasticBuffer combine synchronously at both call sites, so the modular-kernel shared-expert overlap window (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`) is never used: for MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3) the shared-expert FFN serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode.

This PR makes `finalize_async` issue the combine with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`) and return a receiver closure that joins via a device-side `event.current_stream_wait()` — graph-replay safe (the closure keeps `combined_x` and the event alive; no host synchronization inside the captured region).

### Safety

- **On by default** (per review feedback): `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=0` forces the synchronous combine. The flag is read once in `__init__` (never touches `os.environ` inside the captured region). Output is byte-identical either way.
- **DBO**: overlap is disabled under DBO (`dbo_enabled()`), synchronous fallback, log-once.
- **No-event capability gate**: if a DeepEP build returns no combine event, the overlap self-disables permanently (warn-once + a single eager full-sync join) — a pre-capture decision, since warmup always precedes capture; if it is ever hit during capture anyway, a hard `RuntimeError` is raised instead of hiding a sync inside the graph.

### Tests

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_overlap_gate.py` (new, hermetic, no GPU collectives): contract tests for the gate — eager no-event self-disable / capture no-event raise / event-path deferred device-side join. (Ported from a validated harness; the same three contracts pass against this module logic.)
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py`: `test_deep_ep_v2_moe_backends` parametrized over the flag, so the existing torch-reference comparison doubles as the correctness oracle with overlap ON, across eager/cudagraph and both experts backends. That test's MoE has no shared expert, so it also covers the degenerate "async combine with nothing to overlap" path.

### Performance (deployment observation)

DeepSeek-R1-671B FP8, EP8 (2 nodes x TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink), full cudagraphs, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`; pre-registered A/B, 4 independent server starts (ABBA), greedy, forced 128 output tokens, steady-state:

| metric | OFF | ON | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| C=1 decode ITL p50 | 15.71 ms | 14.32 ms | **-8.8%** |
| C=24 decode ITL p50 | 22.05 ms | 20.89 ms | **-5.3%** |
| C=1 TTFT p50 (negative control) | 236.9 ms | 236.8 ms | -0.1 ms |

Greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms. Serving traces: each combine kernel overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs ~9.7 us on average with the flag ON vs exactly 0 OFF. An ablation with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain — the benefit is true overlap. Full evidence in #52744.

### Validation scope

GPU validation was performed on a v0.26.0-era tree; the finalize/combine region is unchanged between v0.26.0 and current main (the dispatch-side drift is unrelated), so the port is mechanical. The contract tests pass against this module logic; the parametrized cudagraph test covers the captured path wherever DeepEP v2 CI runners exist. Default flipped to on per review feedback; the env var remains as an escape hatch.
